printed_value: rounded to the nearest cent before the next step is applied, and a result exactly half way between two cents is rounded to the even cent (p1: to the cent, half to even, at each step)

quotes.text: Rounding to the cent, half to even, at each step

Every amount is ascertained in cents. Where a step of the build-up in Clause 18 produces a fraction of a cent, the result of that step is rounded to the nearest cent before the next step is applied, and a result exactly half way between two cents is rounded to the even cent.

multiplied by the Rig Services Index published for the calendar month in which the service was performed and divided by the base index, rounded half to even. That figure is the rate for the purposes of Clause 17.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: 17A is printed on page 35 (Part IX, Particular Conditions (Second Series)), which is not among the cited pages [1, 6]. Cl.17 frames the step rounding as applying to each step of the Clause 18 build-up.

quotes.text: Where the sum of the amounts of the services charged on an invoice exceeds 250,000.00 USD, the Contractor allows a discount of 4 per cent of the excess
The discount under Clause 38 is calculated on each invoice alone and not on the Contractor's invoices taken together.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: P11 is printed on page 11 (Part VI, Particular Conditions), which is not among the cited pages [8].

quotes.text: the Contractor allows a discount of 4 per cent of the excess, rounded under Clause 17, stated as a single charge under code DS-900 with a negative amount.
The discount under Clause 38 is calculated on each invoice alone and not on the Contractor's invoices taken together.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: P11 (cited in the note) is printed on page 11, which is not among the cited pages [8].

quotes.text: Item DD-120 is charged per circulating hour recorded on the Daily Drilling Report for an Operating day, subject to a minimum of 6 hours on any Operating day on which the tool is in the hole.
DD-120: not less than 6 hours on an Operating day (Clause 21).
The minimum in Clause 21 applies to each Operating day separately and is not averaged over a run.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: P10 is printed on page 11 (Part VI), which is not among the cited pages [6, 22]. Sch 3 Part 7 (p22) states the minimum without the 'tool is in the hole' condition; that condition comes from Cl.21. Ambiguity not resolved here: 21A (p35) makes the first hour of each period in the hole a non-chargeable rig-up hour, and the text does not say whether the 6-hour minimum is measured on hours run or on Chargeable Hours.

printed_value: the first hour of each period in the hole (the invoice charges one fewer)

quotes.text: For a service charged by the hour, the first hour of each period in the hole is rig-up and is not a Chargeable Hour. The report states the hours run; the invoice charges one fewer.
Metres charged not exceeding the metres the report supports by more than 1 per cent are payable as charged. Metres exceeding that are payable at the figure the report supports.

printed_value: 1 per cent for each complete 25 circulating hours the tool accumulated on the well, to a depreciation of not more than 50 per cent

quotes.text: Where a tool cannot be recovered, the charge is its replacement value in Schedule 6 less depreciation of 1 per cent for each complete 25 circulating hours the tool accumulated on the well, as stated on the Lost in Hole Report, to a depreciation of not more than 50 per cent.
Depreciation is 1 per cent for each complete 25 circulating hours, to not more than 50 per cent (Clause 31).
Circulating hours for Clause 31 are those the tool accumulated on the well on which it was lost, including the day of the loss.

are converted into the currency of the Contract at the rate of exchange published in that Schedule for the month in which the tool was lost, rounded half to even, before the depreciation in Clause 31 is applied.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: P12 is printed on page 11 and 31A on page 35; neither page is among the cited pages [7, 25]. 31A does not state the depreciation rate or cap; it governs the base value (Schedule 2D SAR values converted before depreciation, and 'Schedule 2D governs' over Schedule 6), which differs from Cl.31's reference to the Schedule 6 value.

printed_value: A boundary depth belongs to the shallower band.

quotes.text: A boundary depth belongs to the shallower band. Bands end at 1,500 m, 3,000 m and 4,500 m.
Item PD-210 is charged at the rate for the band in which the metres lie (Clause 23). A boundary depth belongs to the shallower band.

discrepancies: Note, not a contradiction: the rule is stated for the measured-depth bands (Cl.23 and the first table of Schedule 2). Schedule 2 Part 2 (metres drilled in the Contract Year, p17) has its own bands printed as '1 m to 40,000 m' and '40,001 m to 120,000 m' and says only that 'an interval that crosses a band is divided at the band'; the boundary-depth sentence is not restated for those bands.

printed_value: any part hour of thirty minutes or more counting as a whole hour

quotes.text: Circulating hours are stated in whole hours, any part hour of thirty minutes or more counting as a whole hour.
